strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with independent iterations
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations where each iteration computes block means, scales, all-reduces the scaled buffer, then unscales. Each iteration is fully independent with 8 all-reduce dispatches total. Straightforward translation of the reference with no fusion opportunities, maximizing clarity at the cost of dispatch count.

strategies.name: Fused mean computation via reduce-scatter
strategies.desc: Replace the implicit global mean computation (sum + divide) with a reduce-scatter that partitions the 8 blocks across ranks, allowing parallel local mean computation, followed by all-gather to broadcast means and a final all-reduce for scaled values. Reduces redundant computation of means across all ranks but increases dispatch count to ~24 (8 iterations × 3 collectives).

strategies.name: Vectorized block operations with single all-reduce per iteration
strategies.desc: Vectorize all 8 block operations (mean, abs, scale) into single tensor operations that process the entire 2048-element vector at once, maintaining the 8 all-reduce dispatches but eliminating loops and enabling better kernel fusion. Trades loop overhead for vectorized compute, keeping dispatch count at 8.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapped all-reduce stages
strategies.desc: Split each iteration's work into compute (mean/scale) and communication (all-reduce) phases, initiating the next iteration's local computation while the previous all-reduce is in flight. Requires async all-reduce primitives and careful buffer management. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but overlaps computation with communication to hide latency.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology by performing node-local all-reduce (within each node's devices) followed by inter-node all-reduce for each of the 8 iterations, potentially using smaller world_size collectives. Increases total collectives to 16 (2 per iteration) but each operates on smaller groups, potentially reducing per-dispatch latency on hierarchical networks.
